summary: BBN's host status report for October 26 to November 5, 1971, with daily test results for each ARPANET host. It was replaced by RFC 267.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 266 reports test results for most Network Hosts from October 26 to November 5, 1971. It says the general status remained as before, and RFC 267 later replaced it.

subtitle: A BBN table of ARPANET host test results from October 26 to November 5, 1971

tldr.problem: Network users needed to know whether most ARPANET hosts could be reached during the reporting period.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists daily connection-test outcomes from the BBN Terminal IMP using codes for open, dead, timed out, half-open and refused.
tldr.outcome: The report says overall host status remained as before and was later replaced by RFC 267.

sections.title: The Host Status Report
sections.content:
RFC 266 reports the status of most Network Hosts from October 26 through November 5. The author says the general status remained as it had been previously.

The table records results of tests from the BBN Terminal IMP and shows the day, date and Eastern time of each observation.
sections.plainLanguage: This report records what happened when most network hosts were tested during the listed period. It says the overall status had not changed from the previous report.

sections.title: Reading the Test Results
sections.content:
O means the host opened a connection and was accessible to users. D means it was dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP; T means it did not respond, although it was not dead. R means it refused the initial request, and H means it opened a connection but immediately closed it or stopped responding.

The report notes that UCLA's IBM-360/91 offered Remote Job Service but did not have a full Telnet server, so the BBN IMP's response was used as an indication that the service was functioning.
sections.plainLanguage: The letters summarize each test: open, inaccessible, timed out, refused, or only partly opened. The report also explains how it interpreted the UCLA system's Remote Job Service response.

sections.title: Scope and Successor
sections.content:
The RFC presents the table as a status snapshot for the reporting period, with individual observations rather than a promise of continuous availability.

The unit metadata records RFC 267 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 266.
sections.plainLanguage: Each table entry is one test result at the time shown. RFC 267 later replaced this report.
